title: Every AI Answer Starts With a Search — and Wall Street Finally Noticed
subtitle: Elastic beat its own guidance across every metric, raised its full-year targets, and watched shares rocket roughly 20% to a fresh 52-week high as search gets priced into the AI trade.
summary: The Search AI Company delivered a clean beat: revenue up 15%, RPO up 27%, record big-customer adds, and raised guidance. Shares popped roughly 20% to a new 52-week high.

bodyHtml:
Every AI answer starts with a search. Before an assistant answers with confidence, something had to dig through billions of records and find the truth. That something is Elastic — "the Search AI Company" — and this week it made a very loud argument that search is the quiet engine underneath the entire AI boom.

Here's Elastic in plain English. Its flagship product, Elasticsearch, is the search engine developers embed inside apps and websites — the software that finds things buried in billions of documents, logs, and messages in milliseconds. On top of that same engine, Elastic sells observability, which watches apps for slowdowns and crashes before customers ever notice, and security, which hunts threats across the network. One engine, three businesses.

Yesterday it was Salesforce's turn, with shares up roughly 20% after a record quarter. Today it's Elastic's. The company reported fiscal Q1 2027 results after Thursday's close, and the market answered with a roughly 20% pop — intraday swings ran from roughly +16% to +29% — sending shares to a fresh 52-week high.

The numbers justify the party. Revenue hit $478 million, up 15% year over year in both reported and constant currency; subscription revenue followed at $449 million, also up 15%. For context, fiscal 2026 finished at $1.7 billion, up 17% — so the top line isn't accelerating; the acceleration is below it. Sales-led subscription revenue climbed 18%, total remaining performance obligations jumped 27% to roughly $1.9 billion, and current RPO rose 21% to just over $1.1 billion.

Customers are the proof. Elastic added a record number of new accounts to its over-$100,000-annual-value cohort, pushing that club past 1,800 members, with net revenue expansion at 111% — existing customers keep buying more. On profitability, non-GAAP operating income hit $77 million, a 16.2% margin, with non-GAAP diluted earnings of 70 cents a share. The GAAP column still shows a $24 million operating loss — stock comp, the usual high-growth tax — so keep the non-GAAP qualifier attached.

The balance sheet is in rude health: $132 million in operating cash flow, $143 million in adjusted free cash flow, $1.5 billion in cash and securities. Then came the part that sent the stock flying — Elastic raised its full-year guidance. Revenue is now guided to roughly $2.0 billion, up about 15% at the midpoint, with a non-GAAP operating margin around 19.4%, non-GAAP EPS just over $3 a share, and an adjusted free cash flow margin near 21.5%. CEO Ash Kulkarni put it plainly: "beating our guidance across all key metrics."

Now the AI thesis, because this is where it gets fun. In late July, Elastic expanded its OpenAI collaboration, pairing Elasticsearch's retrieval, search, and governance with reasoning models so companies can build production AI apps and agents on their own data. That's the R in RAG — retrieval-augmented generation — the mechanism that keeps AI answers grounded in facts instead of hallucinations. Every time an AI assistant cites something real, a search engine did the legwork.

The moves kept stacking. Elastic completed its acquisition of Deductive AI this week, an AI investigation platform that ships an "AI SRE agent" into observability — software that finds the root cause of an outage while you sleep. In late July it pushed agentic security with Attack Discovery, autonomous triage aimed at the industry's "Alert Zero" dream. And back in May, it launched jina-embeddings-v5-omni, letting the same engine search text, images, video, and audio. Search isn't a side quest for Elastic. It's the whole game.

Wall Street got the memo. Thirteen analysts raised price targets on the day, and the stock joined the software rally Salesforce kicked off the day before. It's not all roses — Morningstar still flags long-term structural risk in the search market, and Needham kept its Hold — but the direction of travel is unmistakable.

Here's the bottom line. The market spent two years guessing which software companies AI would eat and which it would crown. Elastic's quarter is a loud argument for the crown. Search is the layer every AI system leans on — the retrieval, the governance, the ground truth — and Elastic just proved it can grow that layer 15% while accelerating the parts that matter most. The Search AI Company isn't waiting for the AI trade. It's building the rails the AI trade runs on.
